events.reader_segment: Small SaaS website owner measuring signup conversion
events.promise: By setting up one signup conversion goal, you can see how many real trial signups you get and which sources and landing pages produce them.
events.arc: Single email: name the gap between a raw signup count and knowing which sources and pages drive real signups, show that one goal closes it, and send the reader to the official guide to see exactly how a goal is set up and read.

emails.job: Get the reader to open the official goal-conversions guide and understand that one signup goal will show them how many real trial signups they get and from which sources and landing pages.
emails.single_idea: Set up one signup conversion goal and your dashboard will show how many real trial signups you get and which sources and landing pages drive them.
emails.objection: Will tracking a signup mean adding code to my site?
must_not_say: Do not name or assume the reader's current analytics tool, and do not pitch switching from Google Analytics
Do not state or assume the reader's traffic volume or pageview tier
Do not assert anything about the reader's privacy or compliance status
Do not present Plausible's own homepage results (84% lift, 2.65%-to-4.80%) as a result the reader will get or as a benchmark for their site
Do not promise to solve trial-to-paid conversion or payment-failure problems — no evidence supports it
Leave pricing, plans and testimonials out; the reader is not evaluating a vendor yet
Do not claim the guide tells them what a 'good' conversion rate is for their traffic

The 2.65% to 4.80% lift (E11) came from Plausible editing its own homepage, not from installing Plausible; the product locates entry pages and drop-off steps and the owner still has to make the change and re-measure.
emails.felt_need: Free-trial signups do not convert to paid at a rate the owner considers acceptable, even after a signup surge.
emails.status_quo: They add free trials that require a payment method upfront to try to convert website visitors into paying customers.
emails.why_it_fails: A raw signup total can be inflated by bot and spam traffic and attributes nothing, so it can't tell the owner which source or landing page is working or how real the spike was.
emails.mechanism: Once Plausible's script is on your site, you mark the page a visitor lands on after signing up as a pageview goal — no extra code. From then on the Goals section reports that goal's conversions broken down by referrer source and entry page, and bot, referrer-spam and data-centre traffic is filtered out of the box so the count reflects real human visits.
emails.next_step_decision: How they would set up or review their own signup goal, and which first page or action to mark as the goal.
emails.next_step_value: On the guide they see exactly how a goal is configured and that the Goals section then reports conversions by source and entry page — so they can picture the setup before installing anything.
emails.next_step_limit: The guide shows how to set up and read a goal; it does not tell them what conversion rate is good for their own traffic, and the breakdowns only appear once the script is live and a conversion has been recorded.

events.body:
One goal can show which sources and landing pages actually produce your trial signups — not just the total.

That goal lives in Plausible Analytics, a privacy-friendly web analytics dashboard. Once the script is on your site, you mark the page a visitor lands on right after signing up as a pageview goal.

Pageviews are collected automatically, so that goal needs **no extra code**. From then on, the Goals section breaks its conversions down by referrer source and entry page.

Bot, referrer-spam and data-centre traffic is filtered out of the box too, so the count reflects **real human visits** — not an inflated spike.

The official goal-conversions guide shows exactly how a goal is configured and what the Goals section reports once a conversion is recorded. You can picture the setup, and which page to mark, before installing anything.

events.message: Email 1, draft 1: "The signup that loads no new page"
events.subject: The signup that loads no new page
events.preview_text: Why a page-based goal can miss the conversions you most want to count
events.body:
Most signup tracking keys on a page load — the thank-you screen, the confirmation URL that appears when someone finishes.

If your signup completes inside the app without ever loading a distinct page, that approach never records it. You end up undercounting exactly the signups you're trying to judge.

Plausible is a privacy-friendly analytics dashboard with two goal types. A pageview goal matches a URL. A **custom event goal** captures the signup as an event sent the moment it fires — through a small snippet or the Events API.

Yes, that event needs a line of code. Once it's in place, the goal reports alongside your traffic sources and entry pages, so you can see which ones bring in real signups.

The official goal-conversions guide walks through how both goal types are set up and what the Goals section reports. Read it and you can pick the one that fits how your own signup flow finishes.

events.subject: Your in-app signups may go uncounted
events.preview_text: A trial signup that never loads a new page can still be tracked as a goal.
events.body:
Signup tracking usually keys on a page load — the thank-you screen, the confirmation URL that shows up when someone finishes.

If your trial signup completes inside the app and never loads a distinct page, that approach never records it. You **undercount exactly the signups** you're trying to judge.

Plausible is a privacy-friendly analytics dashboard, and registering for a trial account is one of the actions its goals are built to track. There are two ways to set that up.

A pageview goal matches a URL. A custom event goal captures the signup as an event sent the moment it fires.

That event comes in through one snippet or the Events API, **added once**. After that, the goal reports alongside your traffic sources and entry pages — so you see which ones bring real signups, not just the total.

The official goal-conversions guide walks through how both goal types are set up and what the Goals section reports. Read it and pick the one that fits how your own signup finishes.
